classificationDefinitions.full-tuition: Covers the specified tuition charges only, subject to award terms. Never labelled a full ride.
classificationDefinitions.full-ride: Covers tuition AND the living or associated educational costs explicitly listed in the award.
classificationDefinitions.full-cost-of-attendance: Covers the institution's defined total cost of attendance, under documented award conditions.
classificationDefinitions.partial: Covers only part of the relevant costs.
classificationDefinitions.unconfirmed: Research has not established the exact coverage or eligibility.

scholarships.name: MIT Scholarship (need-based grant)
scholarships.classificationNote: Institutional need-based aid that aims to meet 100% of demonstrated need. The amount is set per family, is not a fixed sum, and is not guaranteed to every applicant.

coverage.tuition: Covered to the extent of demonstrated need (official aid policy).
coverage.accommodationAndMeals: Part of MIT's cost of attendance used to calculate need (SFS FAQ excerpt); award-level treatment unverified.
coverage.booksAndPersonal: Part of MIT's cost of attendance used to calculate need (SFS FAQ excerpt); award-level treatment unverified.
coverage.livingStipend: Not stated; no separate stipend identified.

eligibility.citizenshipOrResidency: Open to international applicants on the same aid process as domestic applicants (official SFS international page excerpt).
eligibility.nonUsApplicantNote: Applicants from outside the United States (for example from Pakistan, Malaysia, Egypt or Indonesia) follow the same international process. Parental income verification from abroad is required, which may need translation of tax documents (official SFS excerpt).
eligibility.degreeAndProgramEligibility: Undergraduate admitted students. Eligible programmes are not verified per degree family in this build.
eligibility.academicConditions: Not stated as a merit requirement; aid is need-based, not merit-based (official affordability page).
eligibility.renewalConditions: Not verified in detail. Official pages state aid covers the four undergraduate years; GPA and progress rules must be checked.
eligibility.applicantScopeNote: Applies to applicants whose country of citizenship differs from the university's country. Domestic applicants use a different process.
eligibility.programmeScopeNote: Undergraduate admitted students; per-degree eligibility not verified.

requiredDocuments: Parental tax returns or income documentation (translated into English where applicable)
scholarships.applicationMethod: Separately applied for through MIT Student Financial Services, alongside admission.

deadlines.earlyAction: Financial aid application deadline quoted as 30 November (Early Action). Re-check each cycle.
deadlines.regularAction: Financial aid application deadline quoted as 15 February (Regular Action). Re-check each cycle.

scholarships.selectionStatistics: Not verified. Need-based awards are not competitive in the merit sense, but no selection statistics are recorded.
uncoveredCosts: Travel and visa costs (not verified as covered)
Any part of the cost not met by the demonstrated-need calculation
scholarships.verificationNote: The MIT affordability page was fetched directly. The international aid page, FAQ and admitted-student page were read via search excerpts, not full fetches.
scholarships.loansNote: MIT's official aid description states aid is grants and student work expectations and never includes loans (catalog.mit.edu excerpt).
